{"id":8,"answer":"Yes — but only thinly. One saved note is clearly about your DBMS project, and one other note is DBMS coursework that may or may not be the same thing.

- Note 18 (your DBMS project note): records the project idea as a DBMS for personal notes, which should support semantic retrieval rather than keyword search only, with a team of 2. Your attached entry-level guidance says this note is about your own DeepNotes DBMS college project and should be kept separate from Java study material — so treat it as your project note, even though the note text itself frames it as "the professor's project idea."
- Note 21 (DBMS deliverable/reminder): submit the DBMS assignment PDF by Friday 11:59pm on the portal, and include the ER diagram. This is DBMS coursework; the note doesn't say whether that assignment is the project itself or a separate one.
- Possibly related, but not confirmed: note 24 records a meeting with Arjun where retrieval was decided as lexical plus graph, embeddings deferred to v2, and Arjun owning the structure review. It never says the discussion is about the DBMS project, so this is an inference, not a fact from the note.

What is not covered: there is no note on project scope document, milestones, schema/ER design details, or deliverables beyond the team size of 2 and the semantic-retrieval requirement.
